concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) a[i] = a[i] * 10;
concepts.why: The loop variable is used as the index, so each pass writes a different element; the run gives [50, 40, 30, 20, 10].
Each element is read and written through the loop index, which is what makes the change stick in the array.
The standard for header gives i each valid index 0..length-1 exactly once.
a.length is used correctly, but the student says nothing about it.
The student only uses i++ and says nothing about it.
